title: Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4
raw_text:
3.     MOS 2831, Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

    a. Summary. Digital Wideband Systems Maintainers are trained to
install, diagnose, modify, and perform field level maintenance on digital
wideband communications equipment used for high capacity, troposcatter and
satellite link communications. Typical duties include tuning and aligning
systems, adjusting audio or data levels, using test equipment to make checks



                                             3-252                    Enclosure (1)
 3124                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



on circuit quality, diagnose equipment faults to the component level, and
replace faulty parts or components at an organizational or intermediate
maintenance activity. These Marines submit field service maintenance
requests to conduct technical research, order parts, repair, restore and
assist in the installation of Digital Wideband Systems. Journeyman level
Maintainers, with a minimum of three years of experience, reconcile repair
parts and records of systems within the active and maintenance closeout
phases, make recommendations pertaining to maintenance resource allocations
and guide in the installation of digital wideband systems. Additionally,
these Marines provide quality control inspections of maintenance tasks.
These Marines guide novice Marines through non-routine maintenance tasks and
develop competencies of those Marines. Marines in this MOS may be assigned
to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or
more DoD cyber workforce framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference
DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and
certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color vision.

            (3) Must possess an EL score of 110 or higher.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (5) Must have completed one year of high school Algebra 1, Integrated
Mathematics, Mathematical Studies SL, or an equivalent course at the minimum.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Basic Electronics Course (M092721) and the Digital
Wideband Repair Course (M09D3C1) at MCCES 29 Palms, CA.

        (2) Marines must have 36 months obligated service remaining upon
graduation from the Digital Wideband Equipment Repair Course. This obligated
service must be obtained prior to execution of PCS (DUINS) or PCA (DUINS)
orders to the course.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness
Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Radio Mechanics 49-2021.

        (2) Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except
Line Installers 49-2022.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces. The equipment includes various types of communications transmission systems, information technology systems, intelligence processing systems, tactical sensor systems, cryptographic devices, artillery electronics systems, digital fire control systems, unmanned vessel electronics, miscellaneous non-communication systems, robotic and various electro-mechanical systems, electronic jamming systems, and a wide range of test equipment and calibration required devices. Qualifications to work in this field include manual dexterity, normal color vision, be eligible to hold a secret security clearance, the ability to understand highly technical material, and to comprehend complex mathematical and logic principles. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer. Formal schooling is provided to all Marines entering this field. In general, entry-level training consists of basic electronics, electronic systems fundamentals, and an equipment-oriented phase at either a Marine Corps school or other service school. Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field. Skill progression, skill enhancement and skill sustainment training is provided via on the job training and through both distributed learning and formal schooling. Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions. Marines in this field may serve within GCE, ACE, MLG, MIG units and supporting establishments. Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training. Marines entering this field will be assigned MOS 2800, Basic Ground Electronics Maintenance Marine.

matches: Modify, maintain, or repair electronics equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.

The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.

Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer.
Supervise or train other technologists, technicians, or drafters.
Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field.
Install, service, and repair electronic equipment or instruments such as televisions, radios, and videocassette recorders.
Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions.
Teach courses within their department.
Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.

Digital Wideband Systems Maintainers are trained to install, diagnose, modify, and perform field level maintenance on digital wideband communications equipment used for high capacity, troposcatter and satellite link communications.
Inspect and test equipment to locate damage or worn parts and diagnose malfunctions, or read work orders or schematic drawings to determine required repairs.

Typical duties include tuning and aligning systems, adjusting audio or data levels, using test equipment to make checks on circuit quality, diagnose equipment faults to the component level, and replace faulty parts or components at an organizational or intermediate maintenance activity.
Design and oversee testing, installation, and repair of marine apparatus and equipment.
These Marines submit field service maintenance requests to conduct technical research, order parts, repair, restore and assist in the installation of Digital Wideband Systems.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.

Journeyman level Maintainers, with a minimum of three years of experience, reconcile repair parts and records of systems within the active and maintenance closeout phases, make recommendations pertaining to maintenance resource allocations and guide in the installation of digital wideband systems.
Supervise marine engine technicians engaged in the maintenance or repair of mechanical or electrical marine vessels, and inspect their work to ensure that it is performed properly.
Additionally, these Marines provide quality control inspections of maintenance tasks.
Perform general marine vessel maintenance or repair work, such as repairing leaks, finishing interiors, refueling, or maintaining decks.
These Marines guide novice Marines through non-routine maintenance tasks and develop competencies of those Marines.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
